सीकर में इस मानसून सीजन औसत बारिश भी नहीं हुई। आज जिले में हल्के बादल छाए हुए हैं। गर्मी और उमस से लोग परेशान नजर आ रहे हैं। मानसून की ट्रफ लाइन अभी उत्तर प्रदेश और पूर्वी दिल्ली के ऊपर से गुजर रही है। ऐसे में अभी राजस्थान में अच्छी बारिश की कोई संभावना नहीं है।
जिले में इस बार औसत से 8 प्रतिशत कम बारिश हुई है। गर्मी और उमस के कारण तापमान में भी लगातार बदलाव देखने को मिल रहा है।
जिले के फतेहपुर में स्थित कृषि अनुसंधान केंद्र के मौसम विज्ञान केंद्र पर आज सुबह का न्यूनतम तापमान 23.5 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया है। वहीं, सीकर जिले में मंगलवार को अधिकतम तापमान 33.2 डिग्री और न्यूनतम तापमान 23.3 डिग्री दर्ज किया गया। सीकर में पिछले एक सप्ताह से बारिश नहीं हुई है। दिन-रात के तापमान में भी उतार-चढ़ाव देखने को मिला है।
जयपुर मौसम केंद्र के डायरेक्टर राधेश्याम शर्मा ने बताया कि सीकर में अभी सीकर में अच्छी बारिश का कोई पूर्वानुमान नहीं है।

संयुक्त राष्ट्र पर्यावरण कार्यक्रम (UNEP) की नई रिपोर्ट में धरती के बढ़ते तापमान को लेकर चिंता जताई गई है। रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, आने वाले कुछ वर्षों में दुनिया का औसत तापमान 1.5 डिग्री सेल्सियस की सीमा पार कर सकता है। यह पेरिस समझौते में तय अहम सीमा है। देशों के मौजूदा जलवायु वादे पूरी तरह लागू होने के बावजूद तापमान औद्योगिक दौर से पहले के स्तर से 1.8 डिग्री सेल्सियस ज्यादा हो सकता है।
असर
बढ़ते तापमान से क्या होगा असर?
तापमान बढ़ने का सीधा असर ग्लेशियर और बर्फीली चादरों पर पड़ सकता है।
UNE की रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, 2100 तक दुनिया के ग्लेशियर अपने वजन का एक चौथाई से ज्यादा हिस्सा खो सकते हैं। इससे समुद्र का स्तर 9 से 12.5 सेंटीमीटर तक बढ़ सकता है। कई इलाकों में पानी की उपलब्धता भी बदल सकती है।
इसके अलावा, समुद्री बर्फ, पर्माफ्रॉस्ट और बर्फ से जुड़े दूसरे क्षेत्रों में भी बड़े बदलाव देखने को मिल सकते हैं।
खतरा
गर्मी और जंगल की आग बढ़ने का खतरा
रिपोर्ट में कहा गया है कि तापमान बढ़ने के साथ दुनिया में बहुत ज्यादा गर्मी की लहरें और जंगल की आग बढ़ सकती हैं।
समुद्र का स्तर तेजी से बढ़ने और कोरल रीफ जैसे समुद्री तंत्र के खत्म होने का खतरा भी बढ़ेगा। ग्रीनलैंड और पश्चिमी अंटार्कटिका की बर्फीली चादरों में बड़े बदलाव आ सकते हैं।
अमेजन के जंगल और समुद्र की बड़ी धाराओं में भी ऐसे बदलाव का खतरा बढ़ सकता है, जिन्हें वापस बदलना मुश्किल होगा।
जरुरी कदम
तापमान रोकने के लिए क्या करना होगा?
UNEP ने कहा है कि तापमान बढ़ने की रफ्तार कम करने के लिए ग्रीनहाउस गैसों के उत्सर्जन में तुरंत कटौती करनी होगी।
रिपोर्ट के मुताबिक, पहले तापमान को बढ़ने से रोकना और फिर धीरे-धीरे नीचे लाने की कोशिश करनी चाहिए। इसके लिए मीथेन समेत दूसरी गैसों के उत्सर्जन में कमी जरूरी है।
इसके साथ ही, देशों को नेट-जीरो लक्ष्य हासिल करने और हवा से कार्बन हटाने जैसे सुरक्षित उपायों पर भी काम करना होगा।
अन्य
मौजूदा जलवायु योजनाएं क्यों कम पड़ रही हैं?
रिपोर्ट के अनुसार, देशों ने उत्सर्जन कम करने के जो वादे किए हैं, वे अभी पर्याप्त नहीं हैं।
नए राष्ट्रीय जलवायु लक्ष्यों को पूरी तरह लागू करने के बाद भी उत्सर्जन में जरूरी कमी नहीं आएगी। मौजूदा नीतियों के आधार पर 2030 तक वैश्विक उत्सर्जन में बड़ी गिरावट की उम्मीद नहीं है।
UNEP ने कहा कि जलवायु संकट को सीमित करने के लिए देशों को अपने वादों से आगे बढ़कर ज्यादा तेजी और मजबूती से कार्रवाई करनी होगी।

Hyundai Motor Group Pilots 'Nano Cooling Film' on Police Buses Amid Heat Wave
Hyundai Motor Group has applied an advanced material that lowers vehicle cabin temperatures to police buses, aiming to support riot police officers who work long hours in extreme heat.
Hyundai Motor Group announced on the 2nd that it had applied its "Nano Cooling Film" to two Universe police buses belonging to the 1st Mobile Unit at the Seoul Metropolitan Police Agency's Mobile Unit headquarters. The film goes beyond conventional tinting films that partially reflect solar heat by also radiating infrared energy from inside the vehicle outward—a material that Hyundai Motor Group developed as a world first.
Police buses serve as mobile offices and rest, dining, and sleeping quarters at public safety operations such as protests and demonstrations. However, due to regulations and the nature of their duties, dark tinting is difficult to apply, making these vehicles particularly vulnerable to extreme heat. Hyundai Motor Group decided to apply the film after noting that riot police officers have been voicing real difficulties in carrying out their duties during heat waves.
The Nano Cooling Film consists of three layers: two layers that reflect near-infrared wavelengths from solar energy, and one layer that emits mid-infrared wavelengths from inside the vehicle to the outside. It can be attached to vehicles using the same method as conventional tinting films, requiring no separate installation procedures.
The film applied in this pilot has a 90% light transmittance rate and was installed on the side and rear windows of the police buses. The buses were immediately deployed to riot police duties after installation.
Cooling effectiveness was confirmed through comparative testing conducted in-house. In tests Hyundai Motor Group carried out on the Universe FCEV and an ultra-low-floor hydrogen electric bus, vehicles with the film showed cabin temperatures averaging approximately 2–3 degrees Celsius lower than those without, with the sun-exposed driver's seat area dropping by as much as nearly 7 degrees.
Meaningful data was also presented from an energy-saving perspective. On a clear day with an outside temperature of 35 degrees Celsius, approximately 1.6 kWh of electricity is required to lower the Universe's cabin temperature by 1 degree from 27 to 26 degrees. Reducing cooling load through the film can contribute to lower energy consumption and carbon emissions, the company explained.
Through this pilot application, Hyundai Motor Group expects to improve police officers' work performance and achieve energy savings by curbing excessive air-conditioner use. The company plans to track and observe the cooling effect and quality in real police bus operating conditions over the next year before reviewing full-scale mass production.
Lee Min-jae, a senior research engineer at the Hyundai Motor and Kia Basic Materials Research Center who led the Nano Cooling Film R&D, said, "I find it rewarding to have developed a technology that can provide even a small measure of help to police officers struggling in the heat." He added, "We will continue to expand real-world vehicle application cases and conduct follow-up observations to raise the technology's level of completion."
Meanwhile, Hyundai Motor Group previously ran a campaign in Pakistan in 2024—where window tinting is legally prohibited—providing free installation of transparent Nano Cooling Film on the vehicles of more than 70 drivers. Campaigns utilizing the technology have won awards at global advertising festivals including the London International Awards and The One Show.

First Alert Weather Days Wednesday Through Friday

An upper-level high-pressure dome sits stubbornly over the Southeast, keeping our region on the hot. Temperatures in the Upstate reach the mid-90s, with heat index values climbing into the low-100s each afternoon.

The world should brace for more extreme heat in the coming years as global temperatures are expected to cross the 1.5°C threshold above pre-industrial levels.
According to the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP), the best-case scenario would see temperatures peak at 1.8°C above pre-industrial levels, while other scenarios point to warming of more than 2°C.
The rise in temperatures is expected to expose communities and economies to worsening climate risks, increasing the frequency and severity of climate impacts.
The UN in its report explains that warming above 1.5°C will intensify extreme weather and increase pressure on food and water supplies, human health, infrastructure, ecosystems and economies.
Notably, the risks will grow with every additional fraction of a degree and each year temperatures remain elevated, with a rising possibility of more severe heatwaves, wildfires and floods.
Commenting on the findings, UN Secretary-General António Guterres said the increasingly severe weather being experienced around the world offers a warning of the dangers ahead.
“This summer’s scorching heat, raging wildfires and deadly floods are a warning of what lies ahead. We must make the overshoot above 1.5 degrees as small and short as possible. That demands an overshoot of ambition,” Guterres said.
Threat to lives and ecosystems
As warming increases, the report expects more damage to human health, food production, water supplies, nature, cities and infrastructure.
Small Island Developing States and low-lying coastal cities are also expected to face growing risks from rising sea levels.
Higher temperatures could further increase the likelihood of climate tipping points, including the destabilisation of major ice sheets, degradation of the Amazon rainforest and disruption of the Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation, a major ocean system that helps regulate global climate.
The report therefore calls for immediate and sustained cuts in greenhouse gas emissions, including methane, as well as a rapid transition away from fossil fuels towards renewable energy.
UNEP also says countries must strengthen adaptation measures to reduce exposure and vulnerability to the impacts already being experienced and those expected in future.
According to the body, mitigation and adaptation should advance together, with nature-based interventions that can deliver both benefits prioritised.
Carbon dioxide removal will also play an important role in eventually bringing temperatures down, but UNEP warns that it cannot replace deep and sustained emissions reductions.
Carefully governed removal of carbon from the atmosphere will be needed alongside efforts to achieve net-zero and ultimately net-negative emissions.
Hope remains
Despite the worsening outlook, UNEP says the crossing of the 1.5°C threshold does not mean climate goals are lost.
The report identifies an “overshoot, peak and decline” pathway as the best remaining option for limiting the scale and duration of warming above 1.5°C and eventually returning temperatures below the threshold.
Under this pathway, rapid emissions cuts would minimise the temperature peak before long-term net-negative emissions and responsible carbon dioxide removal help reduce temperatures.
UNEP Executive Director Inger Andersen said the window for action remains open, although the response must become faster and more ambitious.
“There are no good outcomes if we remain above 1.5°C. Across the globe, extreme heatwaves are already proving that climate impacts will strike faster, hit harder, and last longer, costing more lives and causing deeper disruption,” Andersen said.
She called for stronger emissions cuts, resilience and adaptation measures while keeping any exceedance of 1.5°C as small and brief as possible.
UNEP adds that political will, international cooperation, climate finance, effective policies and inclusive governance will be critical.

Taipei, Sept. 2 (CNA) Taiwan's Food and Drug Administration (TFDA) on Wednesday issued its highest-level consumer safety alert after U.S. regulators warned that a defect in a temporary heart pump system has been linked to three deaths and 37 serious injuries overseas.
The warning came after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) issued an early notification on Aug. 26 that Abiomed Inc., a subsidiary of Johnson & Johnson, was recalling its Automated Impella Controllers (AICs) due to a cartridge recognition malfunction.
The defect could prevent the controller from confirming whether the cartridge was properly installed, potentially affecting the device's operation, the FDA said.
As of Aug. 17, Abiomed had reported 37 serious injuries and three deaths related to the issue, according to the FDA.
The Impella ventricular support system, described as the world's smallest heart pump, provides temporary circulatory support for patients with severe heart conditions, including cardiogenic shock, as well as those undergoing high-risk procedures such as percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) or coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG), TFDA Medical Devices and Cosmetics Division Director Chien Chia-hung (錢嘉宏) said.
Taiwan has one approved product license for the device, which is used by 19 medical institutions, Chien said. The affected products in Taiwan include 102 purge cassettes, 26 controllers and 97 introducers.
No patient injuries or adverse events related to the defect have been reported in Taiwan, Chien said, adding that the devices are used under close monitoring by medical professionals.
The TFDA has instructed the local license holder, Johnson & Johnson MedTech, to notify healthcare providers and implement the manufacturer's corrective measures, including replacing affected components, updating software and strengthening monitoring procedures.
The agency said it has monitored safety information on the product throughout the year and issued several notices on its website, although none previously involved a recall.
The TFDA's consumer safety alert system uses red, yellow and green levels. A red alert, the highest level, is issued when affected products are available in Taiwan and overseas incidents involve serious injuries or deaths, or when product defects could cause severe harm and require risk-control measures.
